title: Continuation counts over the last two symbols
summary: The model keeps only the last two symbols it read. A table built from training text counts, for every pair of symbols, how often each symbol followed that pair, and the prediction is the most frequent follower of the current pair.
core_idea: Predict the next symbol from counts of what followed the same two symbols in the training text.

state.name: w
state.meaning: The last two symbols read; nothing older is kept.

readout.name: predict
readout.plain: y_hat = argmax over v of T[w_t, v], T the table of continuation counts

learning.description: T[u, w, v] counts how often v followed u, w in the training text; nothing else is learned.
learning.few_shot_argument: A rule that depends only on the last two symbols is learned once each pair has been seen with its follower; the card states 300 examples for a pattern decided by the last two symbols.

cost.why: The complexity claim is stated in n and V; the table is indexed by symbols.

copy.why: The width is the task's symbol count (4 symbols and the separator); the carried state is the last two symbols.

recall.why: The width is the task's symbol count: max(2K, 16) possible keys, 16 values and the separator.

binding.why: 2 hops+2 variable names, 8 constants and the separator.

resources.why: Order c = 3: the carried state is the last two symbols, 2 ceil(log2 d) bits for d symbols; the continuation table is fixed after training.

limits.resources: the carried state w, the last two symbols, 2 ceiling(log2 d) = 6 bits at the copy width d = 5 (64 states)
limits.why: When the separator is read, every later output is a function of the carried state and of the model's own outputs fed back, so exact copying needs a distinct state for each of the D^L strings over D = 4 symbols. The last two symbols take at most 2^6 = 64 values, and 4^L > 64 from L = 4, so two strings share a state and one is copied wrongly.

complexity.constants_notes: Per token: a shift of two symbols and V - 1 comparisons over one row of T. The carried state is two symbols; the table T, V^3 counts, is fixed after training.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Counting continuations of symbol pairs. Example counts m this card states for its learning rule at the solvable cases, each reaching 0.99 on three seeds: 300 for copying at L = 2, 300 for recall at K = 1, 300 for bracket nesting at depth 2 and 300 for two-hop lookup at table size 1. Information account for each count, one target-rule class per task (m counts whole training instances, each with all its scored answers). Copying at L = 2. Class definition: every selector s from the output indices {0, 1} to the source positions {0, 1}; the rule answers at output index i with the source symbol at position s(i), and the target is s(i) = i. Size justification: each of the 2 output indices has 2 choices, so |H| = 2^2 = 4; two different selectors differ at some index i, and a source string with different symbols at the two selected positions gives them different answers. log2 |H| = 2. Recall at K = 1. Class definition: the one stored pair (k_0, v_0) and the one selector s(0) = 0; the rule answers a request for k_0 with v_0, which is also the target. Size justification: with one stored pair there is one selector, so |H| = 1 and nothing about the rule is left to identify. log2 |H| = 0. Bracket nesting at depth 2. Class definition: the six nonempty stack contexts (0), (1), (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), listed bottom to top; every map from these contexts to the two closing tokens, evaluated after each scored prefix; the target maps a context to the closer of its top bracket. Size justification: two choices for each of six contexts, so |H| = 2^6 = 64; all six contexts occur in valid depth-2 prefixes, so different maps give different answers there. log2 |H| = 6. Two-hop lookup at table size 1. Class definition: every selector s from {0} to {0}; given the tables g and f in the input and the request x, the rule answers f(g(s(x))), and the target is s(x) = x. Size justification: at T = 1 there is one selector and one possible answer, so |H| = 1. log2 |H| = 0. Prior bits: 0, relative to these declared classes: the task protocol supplies the token encoding and the restriction to each class, and the mechanism receives no hand-set member of it. This is a restricted-class information bound, not a claim that learning the parsing or lookup operation is free. Bits per example (one whole instance): at most 4 for copying (2 answers over 4 symbols), 4 for recall (1 answer over 16 symbols), 7 for bracket nesting (7 scored closers of one bit), and 1 for two-hop lookup (its one answer carries no information at T = 1; 1 is a loose positive upper bound). The account assumes a target drawn uniformly from each class, so it bounds m from below only; the counts m above are this card's stated claim and are not derived from it.

prediction.statement: 300 examples suffice for a rule decided by the last two symbols.

capabilities.task: copy a string after a separator
capabilities.prediction: Fails for every listed length above 2: the symbol to copy lies more than two tokens back, so at L = 64 over 4 symbols per-string accuracy is at chance, 4^-64.
Fails: the value of a queried item lies more than two tokens back; at K = 64 over 16 symbols per-query accuracy is at chance, 1/16.
Fails whenever the matching opening bracket lies more than two tokens back, which happens at every listed depth from 2; at depth 16 per-sequence accuracy is at most 2^-14.
Fails: the tables lie outside the two-symbol window at every listed size.

falsifiers: A configuration that keeps two symbols copies strings of length 8 exactly.
